In `ReindexDataStreamIndexTransportAction#doExecute` and `ReindexDataStreamTransportAction#doExecute`, the `includeSystem` parameter is set to `true`. This inclusion of system indices in reindexing checks for data streams should be validated against the requirements. If system indices are not supposed to be part of these checks, this might indicate an oversight.

The removal of `getMappingsNodeVersionMetaKey` from `SystemIndexDescriptor` could affect any code relying on this method. Verify that no other parts of the codebase depend on this method and handle its removal appropriately.

The introduction of `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` as an abstract sealed class with `getCurrentResourceName()` and `getIndices(Metadata metadata)` methods requires implementing classes to provide these details. However, the current implementation in `SystemIndexMigrationInfo` does not match the expected behavior for indices migration. Specifically, `getCurrentResourceName()` should return a resource name that is relevant to the system index being migrated, not necessarily the current index name. Similarly, `getIndices(Metadata metadata)` should provide a stream of indices related to the resource being migrated.

The addition of the `includeSystem` parameter in multiple methods and its usage across different classes seems consistent. However, it is crucial to ensure that all call sites of these methods are updated correctly to pass the appropriate value for `includeSystem`. The current changes set `includeSystem` to `false` in most places, which might be intentional but should be verified against the intended behavior.

Changing the visibility of `getSystemIndexDescriptors` from package-private to public is a significant change. Ensure that this method is intended to be part of the public API and that no unintended side effects occur due to increased accessibility.

The use of `TimeValue.timeValueSeconds(1)` could be more descriptive by defining a constant for the delay interval, which would improve readability and maintainability.
In the exception handling within the `ActionListener.wrap`, the error message in `ElasticsearchException` should include the data stream name and feature name to provide more context about the failure.

The method `getCurrentResourceName()` is introduced to `SystemDataStreamMigrationInfo`, which returns the data stream name. However, in `finishDataStreamAndLoop` and `finishResourceAndLoop`, it uses `migrationInfo.getCurrentResourceName()`. This change assumes that all `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` instances will have a `getCurrentResourceName()` method, but only `SystemDataStreamMigrationInfo` has this method. This could lead to a `ClassCastException` if a non-`SystemDataStreamMigrationInfo` instance is passed.

The change from `org.elasticsearch.node.Node` to `Node` is correct if `Node` is already imported. However, ensure that `Node` is indeed imported at the top of the file to avoid any compilation issues.

The change from `SystemIndexMigrationInfo` to extending `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` and the removal of static methods `fromFeature` and `fromTaskState` suggest a refactoring effort. However, the new class `SystemResourceMigrationFactory` introduces a method `getSystemDataStreamsMigrationInfos` that returns a stream containing potentially null values (`null` if `dataStream` is not found). This can lead to `NullPointerException` when processing the stream later on.

The introduction of `getSystemResourceDescriptors` in `Feature` and its usage in `TransportGetFeatureUpgradeStatusAction` are logical. Ensure that this method is used consistently across all relevant parts of the codebase where system resources need to be accessed uniformly.

The change from `org.elasticsearch.cluster.metadata.SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService` to `SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService` assumes that `SystemIndexMetadataUpgradeService` is already imported. Verify that it is imported at the top of the file.

The renaming of methods from `finishIndexAndLoop`, `prepareNextIndex`, and `migrateSingleIndex` to more generic resource-based names (`finishResourceAndLoop`, `startFeatureMigration`, `migrateSingleIndex`) is appropriate if the logic now handles both indices and data streams. Ensure that all method signatures and usages are updated consistently.

In `getReindexRequiredIndices`, `oldIndicesCheck`, and `ignoredOldIndicesCheck`, the `includeSystem` parameter is set to `false`. This implies that system indices are excluded from reindexing checks. Ensure this behavior aligns with the desired functionality, especially if there are scenarios where system indices should be included.

The `getIndices(Metadata metadata)` method uses `Stream.concat` to combine indices from `dataStream.getIndices()` and `dataStream.getFailureIndices()`. Ensure that this operation is efficient and does not introduce performance issues, especially with large datasets. Consider the implications of handling failure indices in the migration process.

The method signature change from `needsToBeMigrated(IndexMetadata indexMetadata)` to `needToBeMigrated(Stream<IndexMetadata> indicesMetadata)` introduces a potential issue where the logic now expects a stream of indices instead of a single index. This change might not be backward compatible with existing callsites that expect a single `IndexMetadata` object. Ensure all call sites are updated accordingly.
The method name change from `needsToBeMigrated` to `needToBeMigrated` is inconsistent with Java naming conventions, which typically use the prefix "is" for boolean methods indicating a condition (e.g., `isNeedsToBeMigrated`). Consider renaming it back to `needsToBeMigrated` or using `isNeedsToBeMigrated`.
The method `needToBeMigrated` now processes a stream of indices, but the assertion and null check inside the lambda are redundant since streams inherently do not contain null elements unless explicitly added. Consider removing these checks if the input stream is guaranteed to be non-null.

The introduction of `ThreadPool` as a parameter and its usage seems consistent across the changes. However, ensure that `ThreadPool` is not being used inappropriately or without proper initialization. Verify that all methods using `threadPool` are thread-safe and that there are no unintended side effects from this change.

The `origin` parameter is being added to the `SystemDataStreamDescriptor` constructor and used in various places. However, there are no checks or validation for the `origin` parameter similar to other parameters like `dataStreamName`, `description`, etc. This could lead to issues if an invalid or null value is passed.

The change in `markAsFailed` method from using `getCurrentIndexName()` to `getCurrentResourceName()` should be verified to ensure it correctly reflects the resource being migrated. This is particularly important for logging and error reporting accuracy.
Ensure that all methods and classes using `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` are correctly updated and that there are no missing or incorrect usages.

The change in `getReindexRequiredPredicate` introduces an additional parameter `includeSystem`. This change affects the behavior of the method and should be thoroughly tested. Ensure that all call sites of this method are updated to pass the correct value for `includeSystem`.

The changes from `SystemIndexMigrationInfo` to `SystemResourceMigrationInfo` in `recordIndexMigrationSuccess` and related methods are consistent with the broader refactoring. Ensure that all necessary changes have been made across the codebase to accommodate this type change.

The introduction of `SystemResourceDescriptor` and its methods adds new responsibilities to classes that implement it. Ensure that all implementing classes provide appropriate implementations for these methods.

The change from `Map.Entry::getKey` to `Entry::getKey` assumes that `Entry` is statically imported or in the same package as `Map.Entry`. Ensure that `Entry` is correctly imported or fully qualified if not.

The removal of the data stream descriptors processing from `getRestoreFromSnapshotAffectedResources` might lead to incomplete detection of affected resources if system indices include data streams. Ensure that this change does not inadvertently skip important checks related to data streams.

The method signature for `getMatchingIndices` has been moved from `IndexPatternMatcher` to a new interface `IndexMatcher`. Ensure that all implementations of `IndexPatternMatcher` are updated to implement `IndexMatcher` as well and verify that any existing implementations correctly override this method if they need specific behavior different from `IndexMatcher`.

The method `getSystemIndicesMigrationInfos` includes an assertion with a detailed error message, which is good for debugging. However, the same level of detail should be applied in `getSystemDataStreamsMigrationInfos`. The current implementation logs less information if a data stream is not found, which might make it harder to diagnose issues.

review_comment:
Could this go into an infinite recursive loop if another part of the system is causing persistent errors? e.g. `migrateDataStream()` -> `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus()` -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` ->  `cancelDataStreamMigration()` -> `migrateDataStream()` -> ...
(I may be missunderstanding the flow control here)

In the original system index migration logic, an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing, such that a user would need to retry.  I spoke with @gwbrown, who mentioned that this was intentional in case there was a failure elsewhere in the system.  WDYT?

It shouldn't. The chain `migrateDataStream()` -> ... -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` is possible if a task for migrating that data stream already exists and is in a failed state. In that case, we cancel it and start a new one.
A new task is only started if the cancellation is successful. This means we shouldn't receive a `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` (line 649), which means that `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus` is called with `restartMigrationOnError=false` (line 647).

There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from `dataStreamMigrationFailed` (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

>an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing

Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

> Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt

Yeah that makes sense and it's a good idea to retry.  

>There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from dataStreamMigrationFailed (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

Exactly.  I'm worried that an issue in some other part of ES might cause this to just loop forever.

review_comment: Should this be at the warn level?

I don't think so. This code should only execute in one scenario: the migration of a data stream starts -> the [child task](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L52) migrating the data stream fails for some reason -> the user restarts the system indices migration task.

Since the data stream migration task [retains](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L295) its status for 1 day, we need to "cancel" the existing task and start a new one to avoid getting the same failure result again. In this case, the failure has already been logged.
"Canceling" the task here is part of normal operation, so I don't think it should be logged as error or warning.  I don't even want to make it info as it might be confusing to see
